plan.angle: Hook (≤15 s): 'On Oct 15, 2026, the EU medicines committee (CHMP) recommended approving orforglipron (Foundayo) for weight management and type 2 diabetes. EMA published this on Oct 16, and the European Commission's final decision is pending. The FDA approved it for chronic weight management on Apr 1, 2026.' Body as planned. The food/water point is credited to the US prescribing information. 'First approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill.' ATTAIN-1 gives per-arm results vs placebo, with group sizes and estimand from NEJM, and no mapping to marketed strengths. ACHIEVE-1 (NEJM 2025) and ACHIEVE-3 (Lilly reported, vs Rybelsus 14 mg) each come with their own population. The side effects beat includes discontinuation vs placebo and the boxed thyroid warning. Comparison with the semaglutide pill: separate trials, no ranking. Prescriber questions, no dosing or switching. Prescriber line.

plan.why: Explainers on named new drugs are the only long videos that travel (median about 30 vs 2.5 for approved drugs). Today's EU news is the hook, and the body rests on peer-reviewed NEJM trials that can be checked in depth. | fact-check: Topic is sound and well within policy. I checked: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) on Apr 1, 2026 for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least 1 weight-related condition. Sources: Lilly/BioSpace press release https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/fda-approves-lillys-foundayo-orforglipron-the-only-glp-1-pill-for-weight-loss-that-can-be-taken-any-time-of-day-without-food-or-water-restrictions and Consultant360 https://www.consultant360.com/fda-alerts/fda-approves-orforglipron-foundayo-chronic-weight-management. The CHMP positive opinion was ADOPTED 15 Oct 2026 and published by EMA on 16 Oct 2026, so the angle's 'Oct 16' date is wrong. Sources: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/foundayo and https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/meeting-highlights-committee-medicinal-products-human-use-chmp-12-15-october-2026. The European Commission decision is still pending. The recommended EU indication is BOTH type 2 diabetes AND weight management (BMI ≥30, or 27 to <30 with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity). Fixes needed: (1) Date correction above. (2) The EMA summary of opinion does NOT mention food or water timing. Attribute 'any time of day, without food or water restrictions' to the US prescribing information (FDA label), not to EMA. (3) Say 'first approved non-peptide/small-molecule GLP-1 pill', not just 'first' (other small molecules, e.g. danuglipron, were tested and dropped). (4) The side-effects beat must include the US label's boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumours (do not use with personal or family history of MTC or MEN2). Use EMA's 'most common side effects are gastrointestinal such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea'. (5) Never map ATTAIN-1 trial doses (6/12/36 mg) to the marketed strengths. Reports list US strengths as 0.8–17.2 mg, so they are not interchangeable. Give trial-arm results only, with no strength or dose guidance. (6) ATTAIN-1 has a 12.4% vs 0.9% placebo figure (top dose, 72 wk). Take each arm's figure, estimand and group sizes from the NEJM paper itself. (7) ACHIEVE-3: check whether a peer-reviewed paper now exists. If not, every number is 'Lilly reported (topline, date)'. Label the comparator 'oral semaglutide (Rybelsus) 14 mg', not 'the Wegovy pill'. (8) Performance note from the playbook: approved-drug long-forms have a median of 2.5 views, and pills are advised as Shorts. Consider whether this long-form slot is worth it.

package.description:
Orforglipron (Foundayo) is the first approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill. Its US label allows any time of day, with no food or water timing rules. US approval (Apr 1, 2026): chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more activity. EU: positive CHMP opinion Oct 15, 2026 (EMA published Oct 16); the European Commission's decision is pending. Stomach side effects are most common, and the US label has a boxed thyroid warning.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
1. Foundayo (orforglipron) US Prescribing Information, Eli Lilly, 2026. https://uspl.lilly.com/foundayo/foundayo.html
2. Foundayo EPAR, CHMP positive opinion 15 Oct 2026, EMA. https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/foundayo
3. Wharton S et al, ATTAIN-1, NEJM 2025. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40960239/
4. Rosenstock J et al, ACHIEVE-1, NEJM 2025. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40544435/

script.working_title: Orforglipron (Foundayo): How Does a Non-Peptide GLP-1 Pill Work? What the Trials Show
script.hook_pattern: Counterintuitive claim + news peg + double open loop: 'A GLP-1 pill that isn't a peptide, with no food or water rules on its US label', then the dated FDA/CHMP status within 15 s, then two puzzles (how a molecule that isn't shaped like GLP-1 switches on the GLP-1 receptor; the one question to ask before comparing GLP-1 pills). Both are paid off later.

scenes.narration: Here's a GLP-1 pill that isn't a peptide, and its US label says you can take it any time of day, with no food or water rules.
scenes.on_screen_text: A GLP-1 pill, no food rules
scenes.retention_device: Pattern interrupt: a GLP-1 that breaks the 'peptide + ritual' expectation

scenes.narration: The FDA approved orforglipron, sold as Foundayo, for chronic weight management on April 1, 2026. Then on October 15, 2026, the EU medicines committee, the CHMP, recommended approving it for weight management and type 2 diabetes.
scenes.on_screen_text: Approved in US, backed in EU
scenes.retention_device: Concrete dated proof point backing the hook

scenes.narration: EMA published that opinion on October 16. The European Commission's final decision is still pending.
scenes.retention_device: Status clarity: what's confirmed vs not yet

scenes.narration: In the US, it's approved for adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related health condition, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity.
scenes.retention_device: Population named early so viewers know if this is about them

scenes.narration: So what makes it different? Every GLP-1 medicine approved before it was a peptide, a chain of amino acids. Orforglipron is the first approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill: a small molecule.

visual.stock_query: amino acid chain beside tiny molecule

scenes.retention_device: Counterintuitive fact that frames the whole video

scenes.narration: In the next few minutes, you'll see why GLP-1 pills were so hard to make, what the big trials actually showed, the side effects worth knowing, and how it compares with the semaglutide pill.

And keep two puzzles in mind. How does a molecule that looks nothing like GLP-1 switch on the GLP-1 receptor? And what's the one question to ask before you compare any two GLP-1 pills? Both answers are coming.

visual.stock_query: curious brain with two question marks

scenes.retention_device: Two open loops: mechanism (mid-video payoff) and comparison question (late payoff)

scenes.narration: To see why this matters, start with the hormone itself.
Your gut releases GLP-1 after you eat. It helps your pancreas release insulin when blood sugar rises, slows how fast your stomach empties, and helps you feel full.

visual.stock_query: gut sending messages to pancreas brain

scenes.narration: But natural GLP-1 is fragile. An enzyme called DPP-4 breaks it down within minutes.

visual.stat_label: How fast DPP-4 breaks down natural GLP-1

scenes.narration: So scientists engineered sturdier peptide versions. Semaglutide, for example, lasts long enough in the body to be injected once a week.
Swallowing a peptide is a whole different challenge. Your digestive system is built to break proteins apart, and large molecules have a hard time crossing the gut wall.
The semaglutide pill, Rybelsus, gets around this with an absorption helper called SNAC, short for salcaprozate sodium.
scenes.retention_device: Mini-solution that sets up a catch

scenes.narration: It works, but it comes with rules. Rybelsus's US label says to take it on an empty stomach with no more than 4 ounces of plain water, then wait at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking or taking other oral medicines.

visual.stock_query: morning kitchen clock and water glass

scenes.retention_device: Concrete contrast that sets up the payoff

scenes.narration: That's a morning ritual. Orforglipron's US label has none of it. So what's different about the molecule?
Picture the GLP-1 receptor as a lock on the surface of your cells.
The natural hormone and semaglutide are long, chain-like keys. They grip the outer part of the receptor and reach into it.

visual.stock_query: long chain key entering cell lock

scenes.narration: Orforglipron is far smaller, more like a typical tablet medicine. Structural studies published in PNAS in 2020 showed it binds in its own way, nestled in a pocket in the upper part of the receptor.

visual.stock_query: tiny key fitting inside lock pocket

scenes.narration: That's the answer to puzzle one: different key, same lock. It still switches the receptor on.

And here's where it gets weird. In those lab experiments, orforglipron acted as a partial agonist, favoring one signaling pathway inside the cell over another. Whether that matters for people hasn't been settled.

visual.stock_query: cell with two paths one brighter

scenes.narration: It was also designed to work when swallowed. Per the US prescribing information, it can be taken any time of day, without food or water restrictions.

visual.stock_query: pill with breakfast lunch dinner plates

scenes.narration: Convenience is great. But it means nothing if the pill doesn't deliver. So let's open the trials.
scenes.retention_device: Question to viewer before chapter change

scenes.narration: The main weight-loss trial is called ATTAIN-1. It was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025.
It enrolled adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, and without diabetes. Treatment lasted 72 weeks, alongside healthy-lifestyle advice.
People were randomized in a 3 to 3 to 3 to 4 ratio: roughly 720 on each orforglipron dose of 6, 12 or 36 milligrams a day, and roughly 960 on placebo, out of 3,127 in total.
The main analysis counted everyone assigned to a group, whether or not they kept taking the pill. That's the more conservative number.
On the 36 milligram dose, average body weight fell by 11.2%. On placebo, it fell by 2.1%.
The lower doses landed in between: 7.5% on 6 milligrams and 8.4% on 12 milligrams.

There's a second way to count, called the efficacy estimand. It estimates the result if everyone had stayed on treatment. By that measure, the top dose averaged 12.4% weight loss, versus 0.9% on placebo.
scenes.retention_device: New angle on the same data

scenes.narration: One caution. Those milligram numbers are trial doses. Don't try to match them to anything at the pharmacy. Dosing is your prescriber's job.
scenes.on_screen_text: Trial doses: leave dosing to prescriber

scenes.narration: So, about 11 to 12% on the top trial dose over 72 weeks. But people with type 2 diabetes are a different story, and that's the next trial.

visual.stock_query: door opening to blood sugar meter

scenes.narration: ACHIEVE-1 was also published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025.

It tested orforglipron in 559 adults with early type 2 diabetes whose blood sugar wasn't controlled with diet and exercise alone: about 140 people on each of three doses, and about 140 on placebo, for 40 weeks.
scenes.retention_device: Population and group sizes up front

scenes.narration: Their average starting HbA1c, a measure of blood sugar over roughly three months, was 8.0%.

visual.stock_query: red blood cells with sugar cubes

scenes.narration: After 40 weeks, HbA1c dropped by 1.24 to 1.48 percentage points across the orforglipron doses, compared with 0.41 on placebo.
Weight fell too: 4.5% to 7.6% across the doses, versus 1.7% on placebo. That's a different population and a shorter trial than ATTAIN-1, so don't line those numbers up against each other.
scenes.retention_device: Plants the comparison theme for puzzle two

scenes.narration: Then came the comparison people really wanted: one GLP-1 pill against another.

ACHIEVE-3 tested orforglipron head-to-head against oral semaglutide, Rybelsus, including the 14 milligram dose. It enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes whose blood sugar wasn't controlled on metformin, and ran for 52 weeks.

visual.stock_query: two pills side by side race

scenes.narration: In the published results, in The Lancet in 2026, orforglipron lowered HbA1c and body weight more than Rybelsus 7 and 14 milligrams over 52 weeks. The trial was open-label, and stomach side effects, and stopping because of side effects, were more common with orforglipron.
scenes.on_screen_text: Lower HbA1c and weight, more stomach side effects

scenes.narration: That's the good news. Now, what does it cost your stomach?
Orforglipron has side effects worth knowing about before you start.
EMA says the most common side effects are gastrointestinal, such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
In ATTAIN-1, stomach side effects were the most common, and most were mild to moderate.
Some people stopped because of side effects: from 5.3% to 10.3% across the orforglipron doses, compared with 2.7% on placebo, over 72 weeks.

visual.stat_label: Stopped for side effects, vs 2.7% placebo

scenes.narration: Then there's the boxed warning on the US label: a risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, a warning GLP-1 medicines carry because of findings in animal studies.
Orforglipron shouldn't be used by anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or a genetic condition called MEN 2. If that's you, make sure your prescriber knows.
scenes.on_screen_text: MTC or MEN 2 history? Tell them

scenes.narration: The label lists other warnings and precautions too, so go through the full list with whoever prescribes it.

If nausea shows up, smaller meals, eating slowly and stopping as soon as you feel full can make it easier. And if side effects don't settle, call your prescriber rather than changing anything yourself.
Which brings us to the question everyone asks: is it better than the semaglutide pill?

visual.stock_query: two pills on podium question mark

scenes.retention_device: Sets up payoff of open loop #2

scenes.narration: Here's the answer to puzzle two. Before you compare any two GLP-1 pills, ask one question: were they tested in the same trial?

visual.stock_query: chapter card two pills one arena

scenes.retention_device: Payoff of the main open loop #2

scenes.narration: For people with type 2 diabetes, ACHIEVE-3 is that same-trial comparison. Orforglipron lowered blood sugar and weight more than Rybelsus 14 milligrams, with more stomach side effects.

visual.stock_query: two pills in one race track

scenes.narration: For weight loss in people without diabetes, the 25 milligram semaglutide pill was tested in its own trial, called OASIS 4, with different people, a different length and a different design from ATTAIN-1.

It's tempting to put those two weight numbers side by side. But separate trials enroll different people and count results differently, so they can't tell you which of those pills is better for weight.

visual.myth: Bigger number in its own trial means better drug
visual.fact: Only same-trial comparisons can rank two drugs

scenes.narration: What you can say is that they're built differently. Rybelsus is a peptide with an absorption helper and strict timing rules on its US label. Orforglipron is a small molecule with no food or water restrictions on its US label.

items: Orforglipron: small molecule, no food rules

scenes.narration: For some people, that convenience matters a lot. For others, cost, coverage, side effects or other health conditions matter more. That's a conversation for your prescriber.
If you and your prescriber decide on any GLP-1 medicine, a few habits are worth building alongside it.
Include protein at each meal to support your muscles while you lose weight. If you have kidney disease, check with your doctor before upping your protein.
WHO recommends muscle-strengthening activity on two or more days a week for adults. If you're new to it, start gently and build up.
Sip fluids through the day, especially if you've had vomiting or diarrhea, unless you've been told to limit fluids.
And remember, in the US it's approved alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, not instead of them.

visual.stock_query: pill walking with sneakers and salad

scenes.narration: Last thing before we wrap: what to actually say at your appointment.
scenes.retention_device: Open loop into final practical section

scenes.narration: Here are four questions worth bringing.
One: is orforglipron a good fit for my health, my goals and my other conditions?

items: How does it fit my medicines?
Which side effects need a call?

scenes.retention_device: Numbered list keeps viewers to the end

scenes.narration: Two: do I have any personal or family history that rules it out, like medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2?
Three: how does it fit with the medicines I already take? Bring the full list. If you're on another GLP-1 or a diabetes medicine, don't stop or change it on your own. Decide together.
Four: which side effects should I expect, which ones mean I should call you, and when will we follow up?
Also mention if you're pregnant, planning a pregnancy or breastfeeding, and ask about coverage, because access to a new medicine can vary by country and by plan.
So let's pull it all together.
Orforglipron looks nothing like GLP-1, yet it switches on the same receptor by fitting into it in its own way. Different key, same lock.
In ATTAIN-1, the top trial dose averaged 11.2% weight loss over 72 weeks, versus 2.1% on placebo, in adults with obesity or overweight and without diabetes.
Stomach side effects are the most common, there's a boxed thyroid warning on the US label, and only same-trial comparisons can rank it against other pills.
As of October 17, 2026, it's FDA-approved for chronic weight management, and the EU decision is pending after a positive CHMP opinion.

visual.stock_query: calendar with US and EU flags

scenes.narration: Your quick checklist: small molecule, same receptor. No food or water rules on the US label. Stomach side effects most common. A boxed thyroid warning. And compare pills only within the same trial.

factcheck.summary:
Content check of the long-form "Orforglipron (Foundayo): How Does a Non-Peptide GLP-1 Pill Work?": PASS, with three small fixes.

What I checked against sources:
- **Regulatory status:** FDA approval on Apr 1, 2026 for adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity. CHMP positive opinion on 15 Oct 2026 for type 2 diabetes and weight management, published 16/10/2026. The European Commission decision is still pending. All confirmed.
- **ATTAIN-1:** 3,127 people randomized 3:3:3:4, without diabetes, 72 weeks. Weight change was −7.5%, −8.4% and −11.2% on 6, 12 and 36 mg vs −2.1% on placebo, and −12.4% vs −0.9% by the efficacy estimand. Stopping for side effects was 5.3–10.3% vs 2.7%, and stomach side effects were mostly mild to moderate. All confirmed.
- **ACHIEVE-1:** 559 people randomized 1:1:1:1 on 3, 12 or 36 mg or placebo, diet and exercise alone, 40 weeks, starting HbA1c 8.0%. HbA1c fell 1.24–1.48 points vs 0.41, and weight fell 4.5–7.6% vs 1.7% (treatment-regimen estimand). All confirmed.
- **ACHIEVE-3:** Lancet 2026, open-label, 52 weeks, metformin background. Orforglipron 12 and 36 mg vs Rybelsus 7 and 14 mg, with greater HbA1c and weight reductions. Stomach side effects were 58–59% vs 37–45%, and stopping for side effects was 8.7–9.7% vs 4.5–4.9%, so the script's trade-off framing is accurate.
- **PNAS 2020 (Kawai):** orforglipron is a partial agonist with no detectable β-arrestin recruitment (it signals through one pathway, not the other), and it binds in its own pocket in the upper part of the receptor. Confirmed.
- **Labels:** the US label (revised July 2026) says once daily with or without food, carries the thyroid C-cell boxed warning, and rules out use with MTC or MEN 2 history. The Rybelsus rules (empty stomach, up to 4 oz water, wait 30 minutes) are correct. OASIS 4 (NEJM 2025, Wharton) exists.

Framing and safety are good: populations are named, the effect counted for everyone assigned comes first, separate trials aren't ranked against each other, the trial-dose warning is there, and the kidney, fluids, exercise, don't-change-medicines, pregnancy and prescriber lines are all present.

The three fixes:
1. **s45:** the boxed-warning line says all GLP-1 medicines carry this warning, which isn't true of every one. The label also says orforglipron itself isn't active in rodents and the risk to people hasn't been determined.
2. **Source S1:** the Lilly investor URL returned 403 (blocked), so I couldn't confirm it.
3. **s39 on-screen text:** it drops "open-label" and is long. Optional fix.

issues.claim: a risk of thyroid C-cell tumors, a warning GLP-1 medicines carry because of findings in animal studies
issues.problem: This overgeneralizes. Not every GLP-1 medicine carries this boxed warning, and the Foundayo label says the tumors were seen in rodents given other GLP-1 receptor agonists. Orforglipron isn't pharmacologically active in rodents, and whether the risk applies to people hasn't been determined.
issues.fix: Replace the narration with: "Then there's the boxed warning on the US label: a possible risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. It's based on rodent studies of other GLP-1 medicines, and whether it applies to people hasn't been determined."

issues.claim: Lilly investor news release URL for the FDA approval
issues.problem: The URL returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so I couldn't confirm it resolves. The craft rules exclude 403 and redirect URLs. FDA approval facts are also supported by S2, the US prescribing information.
issues.fix: Swap S1 for the canonical lilly.com news-release URL of the same April 1, 2026 release if it resolves. Otherwise drop S1 and cite S2 in s01, s02, s04, s05, s15, s60 and s72. Note that s05's 'first approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill' line then needs a working Lilly or FDA source.

issues.claim: Lower HbA1c and weight, more stomach side effects
issues.problem: The on-screen text leaves out the comparator and the open-label design that the narration gives, and it's long for one card.
issues.fix: Change on_screen_text to: "Vs Rybelsus: lower HbA1c and weight, more stomach side effects (open-label)"

thumbnail.reasoning: All three are legible at phone size with a single clear focal point (the pill mascot) and brand-consistent colors. #2's "EU STEP CLOSER" pivots to a regulatory-news hook that isn't promised by the title ("no food rules") — it could pull clicks from people expecting regulatory news, then lands on a mechanism explainer, creating a mild bait/mismatch risk even though factually it stays hedged ("closer" not "approved"). #0's "HOW IS IT DIFFERENT?" is clean and on-topic but is pure curiosity with no concrete payoff cue, which per the playbook (named drug/number/milestone outperforms generic curiosity) likely underperforms. #1 "1ST" + "NON-PEPTIDE GLP-1 PILL" gives a concrete, credible milestone that directly ties to the title's "first" framing and the mechanism hinted at by "no food rules," while still leaving the "why/how" curiosity open. It's legible, has the strongest focal anchor (bold numeral + explicit descriptor), and best matches our proven pattern of pairing a credible specific claim with curiosity.

issues.claim: Orforglipron (Foundayo) is the first approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill. In the US it's approved for... Its US label allows any time of day, with no food or water timing rules.
issues.problem: The quick answer is about 5 sentences, but the rule is 3 lines or fewer. It also mentions only benefits and convenience: none of the common side effects or the boxed warning from the verified script appear in this field.
issues.fix: Orforglipron (Foundayo) is the first approved non-peptide GLP-1 pill. Its US label allows any time of day, with no food or water timing rules. US approval (Apr 1, 2026): chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more activity. EU: positive CHMP opinion Oct 15, 2026 (EMA published Oct 16); the European Commission's decision is pending. Stomach side effects are most common, and the US label has a boxed thyroid warning.
